findings_addressed.oracle: Controlled env file with exactly one synthetic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. After loader construction (which calls _load_env_file and populates os.environ), the test strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from os.environ before calling reload(). This closes the os.environ fallback that _get_var() uses: if reload() clears _env_vars but does not re-read the file, both _env_vars and os.environ lack the key, so list_configured_providers() returns [] and the post-reload assertion fails.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In CredentialLoader.reload() (env_loader.py), remove the call to self._load_env_file() so the method only executes self._env_vars.clear(). After that mutation: _env_vars is empty; os.environ no longer has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (stripped by the test between init and reload); _get_var() returns None; list_configured_providers() returns []; ProviderName.ANTHROPIC not in after is True; the post-reload membership assertion fails.
findings_addressed.adversarial_reviewer_weakness_addressed: _load_env_file() (called by __init__) copies ANTHROPIC_API_KEY into os.environ as a side-effect. The prior version cleared os.environ only BEFORE loader construction, so __init__ immediately re-populated it. A broken reload() could satisfy _get_var() via os.environ.get() even with an empty _env_vars. The fix: strip ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from os.environ AFTER loader construction (after the 'before' snapshot) but BEFORE reload(), so the only legitimate post-reload source is the file re-read inside reload() itself.

The fix adds os.environ.pop(anthropic_var, None) after loader construction but before reload(), ensuring the _get_var() os.environ fallback cannot satisfy the post-reload lookup if reload() fails to re-read the env file.
